answers.answer: Keep 4 tokens of each gem color and 5 gold. Reveal 3 nobles; remove all unrevealed nobles permanently.
answers.evidence: Setup table: "2 | 4 (remove 3 of each color) | 5 | 3". Setup: "Remove remaining noble tiles from the game -- they will not be used."

answers.answer: Three players: 5 gems per color, 5 gold, 4 nobles. Four players: 7 gems per color, 5 gold, 5 nobles. Four players therefore add two gems per color and one noble, with gold unchanged.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments table: "3 | 5 (remove 2 of each color) | 5 | 4"; "4 | 7 (use all) | 5 | 5".

answers.answer: Shuffle each level deck separately. Place them in a column with level 1 at bottom, level 2 in middle, level 3 on top. Reveal four cards per level for a 3-by-4 market. The youngest player starts; play proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup: "Shuffle each ... separately"; "Level 1 at bottom, Level 2 in middle, Level 3 on top"; "Reveal 4 cards ... from each level". First Player: "The youngest player goes first. Play proceeds clockwise."

answers.answer: Take three different gems; take two gems of one color; reserve a development card and take one gold; or purchase a development card. You cannot take gems then buy, or reserve then buy that card, on the same turn: each would require two actions.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: "must perform exactly one of the following four actions" followed by all four choices.

answers.answer: Unsupported: the summary does not specify what information about owned tokens must be visible to opponents or when.
answers.evidence: No owned-token visibility rule appears. The Purchase section visibility rule concerns card "bonuses and prestige point values".

answers.answer: You may take two green, leaving two. You may not take two red. Check the supply before removing the tokens: it must contain at least four of the chosen color when taking them. Neither gem-taking action permits gold.
answers.evidence: Same-color action: "at least 4 tokens of that color in the supply when the player takes them"; "If a color pile has 3 or fewer tokens, you cannot take 2 from it." Both gem-taking actions: "You may not take gold tokens with this action."

answers.answer: You may temporarily reach twelve when taking the gems, but must immediately return two tokens to finish at ten. They may include tokens just drawn. Gold counts toward the limit.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: "more than 10 tokens (including gold) at the end of their turn" is forbidden; "immediately return tokens of their choice ... until they have exactly 10"; "may return tokens they just took."

answers.answer: Take the reserved card and one gold, temporarily reaching eleven tokens. Immediately return one token of your choice, possibly that gold, to finish at ten. If gold is empty, still reserve the card, receive no gold, and remain at ten.
answers.evidence: Reserve: "also take 1 gold token"; "If no gold tokens remain, you may still reserve a card but receive no gold." Token limit: "return tokens of their choice" and "may return tokens they just took."

answers.answer: Reserve a face-up market card or the top card of any one of the three level decks. A card taken from a deck is not shown to opponents. Only the player who reserved a card can buy it.
answers.evidence: Reserve: "A face-up development card from the 3x4 grid" or "The top card from any one of the three level decks, without revealing it to other players"; "Reserved cards may only be purchased by the player who reserved them."

answers.answer: You cannot reserve while already holding three reserved cards, even if you want only gold. You cannot discard or exchange a reserved card to make room; purchasing it is the only way it leaves your hand. Gold can only be obtained by reserving a card.
answers.evidence: Reserved Cards: "If a player already has 3, they cannot reserve another"; "The only way to remove a reserved card from your hand is to purchase it." Gold: "can only be obtained by reserving a development card."

answers.answer: Immediately refill the level-2 space with the top card of the level-2 deck. Purchasing a face-up card uses the same immediate replacement. Buying a reserved card takes it from your hand, so creates no market gap to refill. If the corresponding deck is empty, a market gap remains empty for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Card Replacement: "Whenever a face-up card is acquired (purchased) or reserved from the grid, it is immediately replaced by the top card of the same level's deck"; empty deck: "empty space ... remains empty for the rest of the game." Purchase permits a "previously reserved card from your hand."

answers.answer: Spend one green and no blue tokens; a gold can substitute for that green. If bonuses cover every required color, spend no tokens. Bonuses are permanent and are not spent.
answers.evidence: Payment example: "if a card costs 2 blue and 1 green, and you have 2 blue bonuses, you only need to spend 1 green token." Gold substitutes for any gem. Bonuses are "permanent" and can allow purchase "without spending any tokens at all."

answers.answer: Yes. After bonuses the remaining cost is one blue, one black and one white. Pay the blue token for blue and one gold each for black and white. Return all three spent tokens to the supply. Keep your bonus cards and their permanent bonuses.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: bonuses reduce tokens required; "Gold tokens (jokers) can substitute for any single gem token"; gem tokens and spent gold return "to the supply." Bonus Stacking: each purchased card adds a bonus "permanently."

answers.answer: Buy a face-up market development card or one previously reserved in your own hand. Arrange purchased cards face up in front of you, sorted by bonus color and staggered so bonuses and prestige values remain visible to all players at all times.
answers.evidence: Purchase: "a face-up development card from the grid or a previously reserved card from your hand"; "Place purchased development cards face-up in front of you, sorted by bonus color and staggered so that bonuses and prestige point values are visible to all players at all times."

answers.answer: You do not qualify with only two white bonuses: a white or gold token cannot supply a bonus. Acquiring a third white bonus meets all requirements, qualifying you at the end of your turn. Extra bonuses do not disqualify you.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: "at least the quantity and types of bonuses (from purchased development cards) shown"; "bonuses only ... not gem tokens." Noble Tile Mechanics: "having more is fine."

answers.answer: Choose one noble; you cannot take both or decline all visits. The other remains available. The visit uses no action, gives three prestige points, and is checked at the end of your turn after the action and token-limit check.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: "automatic -- a player cannot refuse it"; "not an action"; "choose one"; "at most one noble per turn"; "3 prestige points." Turn Structure: check "10-token hand limit and then ... noble visit."

answers.answer: Unsupported: the summary does not say where a received noble tile is placed or whether it is face up or hidden.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits covers receiving a tile and its points, but gives no placement or face-up/hidden instruction.

answers.answer: C and D take their turns before the game ends. A does not take another turn, so all finish with equal turns. B is not guaranteed to win; another player may surpass B, and the highest final prestige wins.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: "the current round is completed so that every player has played the same number of turns." Clarifications: the triggering player "may not necessarily win if another player surpasses them in the same final round."

answers.answer: Your total becomes sixteen. That triggers the end because the threshold is fifteen or more, even if you skipped fifteen. Finish the current round, then determine the winner by final prestige and the tiebreaker if necessary.
answers.evidence: Nobles: "3 each." End-Game Trigger: "15 or more prestige points" and "current round is completed." Winner: "most prestige points at the end of the final round."

answers.answer: B wins: A and B tie for highest prestige at sixteen, and B has nine purchased developments versus A's ten. C has fewer points, so the tiebreaker cannot help C. Nobles count toward prestige. B's three reserved cards are not purchased developments and do not count for that tiebreaker.
answers.evidence: Winner: "most prestige points" and "Noble tile points count toward the total." Tiebreaker: player who "has purchased the fewest development cards." Reserved cards leave the hand only by being purchased.
